Workflow

How agents work on this team.

Only the label changes: its agents, tasks and history stay.

Changes the name people see. Its agents, tasks, history and links stay the same.

Instructions are saved with each task when it is first claimed.

Tasks already claimed keep their instructions. This setting gives guidance; it does not create worktrees by itself.

Team working modes

No extra guidance.

Tells agents how to work when a task waits on another.

When an agent needs another agent to do something, it creates a task. Plain posts are for questions and status.

Every new task needs a goal, and a task cannot be moved to no goal.

Team-specific conventions, given to agents with each task.

A preset saves with Save preset, not Save settings.

Health check

When an agent that stopped working is noticed.

Team health checks are turned off for all of Coral, so this team's check will not run. Turn on "Team health checks" in . It takes effect after Coral restarts.

Checks on stuck or idle agents. Uses tokens each time.

minutes

So a quiet team is not mistaken for a stopped check.

Reviews

When a task is submitted for review and nobody is assigned, Coral delegates it to the default reviewers; with none named, reviews wait for the orchestrator. Works whether or not the health check is on.

Names of agents on this team, up to 8, separated by commas.

Automatic rules

Run only while the health check is on.

An agent that is idle with ready work gets a reminder; past the count, the orchestrator is told.

minutes idle

nudges

An agent that has done nothing for a while is asked where it stands; if it stays quiet, the orchestrator is told.

minutes quiet

minutes later

A message Coral could not type into an agent (its terminal is on a dialog) and has held back for a while is reported to the Operator.

minutes held

A message that @mentions the orchestrator and has had no reply gets a reminder.

Work done off the books

Named to the orchestrator in the next health check, once each.

An agent that has been working for a while with no task in progress is named in the next health check, once.

minutes

A commit, SHA or patch posted on the board with no task number, by an agent with no task in progress, is named in the next health check, once.

An artifact uploaded by an agent with no task in progress (and not marked as having no task) is named in the next health check, once.

A goal that is not closed and has more tasks than the limit (open and done together) is named in the next health check, and again at each further limit.

tasks in a goal

Landing

Finished work that has not landed. Reads the local branch only, never CI or GitHub.

Landing

Messaging

How the team's messages reach its agents.

This team was made before Coral Hub links existed, so it cannot use the relay.

Message teams here: off

Coral Hub can change these settings.

How this works

Messaging and file sharing with teams on other computers go through Coral Hub links. Another team can message this team only when its Coral Hub account has linked the two teams and cross-team messaging is on here. That switch is on unless you turn it off: it is a kill switch, and the link is the permission. Linking happens in Coral Hub (Team links). Messages from other teams are requests, not instructions. Files are shared only while Share files with other teams is on; they are not scanned, and artifact bytes are not redacted.

The system preview includes the board introduction; the action preview resolves the board placeholder. These are separate launch channels, not one concatenated prompt.
